# The Holograph

A reading system can hand its consumer a small pattern in place of the material, but only if the pattern can be opened back into the material by someone other than the consumer.

That sentence is the whole bet, and this essay tries to say what it commits the instrument to, where it came from, whether its visible half could be the heart of the fold, and why the same commitment holds when the material is a score or a photograph instead of a novel. The finding I want to defend is narrower than the name suggests. The holograph is not a compression technology and it is not a summary a model wrote. It is an addressing technology with a rule about who may hold the addresses, and what a person or a mouth reads from it is a summary that can be reopened. Everything that sounds like a feature, the flat prompt cost, the exact provenance, the medium blindness, falls out of that rule.

A note on the ground this stands on. I read `THE-HOLOGRAPH.md` and its neighbours in a public clone of eoreader7 at `fffac86` (Oct 5). The canonical copy under `scores-patch-points` needs auth I do not have, so anything below that depends on the newest head is unverified, and the document's own pending numbers are still pending. Section 6 was added on Oct 5 after reading the mechanical summary code and the Sept 25 pilot, and it is the least settled part of the essay.

## 1. The record is the object

The claim in the repo is that the record is the object and what any consumer is handed is a small pattern computed from it. A few addressed holons, each standing in for the material it was computed from, from which any part of the whole can be re-expanded by the record, never by the consumer.

Three properties separate this from a summary. Every part points at the whole: each line the record produces carries an address into the record, a byte range, a turn, a note's witnesses, and the record can expand it to the bytes, the claims around them, the referent's whole neighbourhood. Abstraction compresses: a Lens line, a claim with its standing, stands in for the sentence it was read from; a Paradigm line, an act that recurs between two referents, stands in for every occurrence; an Atmosphere line stands in for the run of exchanges it was computed over. And the consumer never gets the addresses. The pattern reaches the mouth with every address struck, in one wall at the mouth's door, `firewall.js::mouthFacing`, and the record reattaches them to the answer afterwards, mechanically, in `cite.js`.

The third property is the odd one, and it has the best origin story. It was a law before it had a name. A model was told to cite addresses and produced a fabricated "[4]". A model handed an address will write one, and a written address is a fabrication order. So the address became the record's to attach, and the mouth was reduced to voicing a pattern it could not point from.

The consequence the design bets on is that the size of what the mouth sees stops depending on the size of the material. A novel and a shelf of them cost the same few hundred tokens a turn, because the reading happened once, at admission, and a turn is a query over it cut where widening stops changing anything.

## 2. How a turn works

A question activates referents. Its own, resolved through the referent index, or the last answer's when it names none. The activation spreads one hop over what the record holds about them: the mentions the index established, every sentence where an active referent stands, with its address, and the notes whose ends resolve to them. Those sentences are the ground. They are ranked by hop and by how many active referents they carry, and cut where showing one more changes nothing about what the question reaches.

So retrieval is not a step before reading. It is a query over the reading. That is the structural difference from chunk retrieval, where a string matcher scores containers that were cut for the matcher's convenience. Here the unit is the sentence, because that is what the organs read, the reach is the neighbourhood, because that is what a referent is, and the cut is measured, because a hand-picked count of chunks was the one number in the turn that nothing had earned.

Two places in that account were wrong the first time, and both are on the record. The shared cut had offered the whole candidate set as one of its own depths, and a set whose every row carries a distinct act agrees with itself, so the "measured" window was the ceiling wearing a measurement's face. The Lens handed 94 lines about one referent; the sentence window rode its 48-sentence ceiling on every question of three runs. The fix was to stop offering the whole set as a rung, and when no rung reproduces the reach, to hand the top of the ladder and call it a declared ceiling. Then the compression driver turned out to have run every question against an empty transcript, so a follow-up that named no referent bound to nothing. Threaded with the run's own transcript, 20 of 25 questions activate, and level 1 sits at its 24-sentence ceiling on all of them, a fact the first driver never disclosed. The ladder does compress, 4,287 characters of sentences at level 1 against 605 at level 3 on one run, but it names the places where it cannot.

## 3. What it is not, and one mistake about what it is

It is not retrieval-augmented generation, which hands a model raw chunks and lets the model read them. The holograph hands computed readings, resolved by identity, cut by a measured window, with the addresses held back. The model reads nothing. It voices.

It is not a summary a model wrote. The one place a model used to read the discourse whole, the refresh call that wrote the fold's topic and flow, is exactly what the Atmosphere block replaces, computed from referent sets per exchange.

And it is not an organ. I got this wrong earlier in the work, treating the holograph and the hyperlexicon as two halves of one thing, and the cube corrected me. The hyperlexicon is an organ, a cell with a stance, the only occupied Generate cell. The holograph has no operator. It is a law over what the Figure and Pattern columns may hand downward. Asking whether they merge is like asking whether a verb should merge with grammar. The repo later named the pair apart: the holograph is per source, the record of one text's reading; the hyperlexicon is where cross-reading knowledge accumulates and primes the next read. The holograph is a whole to its addresses, and the hyperlexicon is a part to the whole corpus, the same holon one level up.

That also gives the pair a symmetry worth keeping. The holograph guards the downward side of a wall: a pattern may be handed over because the record can reopen it, and the consumer may never author what it receives. The hyperlexicon guards the upward side: adjacency may nominate, and only a named giver may license. Same prohibition, opposite directions, and neither module imports the other.

## 4. Prior art, broken at the joint

The name is a metaphor with a real ancestry, and the useful way to read the ancestry is to find where each ancestor stops fitting.

[Gabor's holography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dennis_Gabor) records an interference pattern from which the whole image reconstructs, and any fragment of the plate reconstructs the whole at lower resolution. [Pribram's holonomic brain theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holonomic_brain_theory) carried that into memory. The instrument keeps the shape and refuses the physics: a fragment of the record reconstructs the whole through its address, not through superposition. That is the first joint, and it matters because superposition is lossy and addressing is not.

The nearest technical use of the word is [Plate's holographic reduced representations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyperdimensional_computing), which bind structures into fixed-width vectors by circular convolution and recover components approximately. The repo states the difference exactly: an HRR recovers approximately from a superposition, the holograph recovers exactly from an address. The name is kept for the property that every part carries the whole, and the mechanism is rejected wherever the record already has something lossless.

The associative lineage, [Hopfield's content-addressable networks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hopfield_network) and [Kanerva's sparse distributed memory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sparse_distributed_memory), is not rejected. It is used, in the keyless field of `relative.js`, a 4,096-bit sparse representation with a measured null band. The repo splits it into three tiers by how much of the residue survives: the holograph proper, the record merged, full tokens and the address, the only tier the mouth reads; the shadow, state plus address with no words, recall only; and the echo, 512 bits, "something like this was said here," sealed and never read back into the notation.

The hypertext line is the direct ancestor of addresses over restated text. [Bush's memex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memex) and [Nelson's transclusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transclusion) are inclusion by reference rather than by copy. A line in a block is a transclusion the mouth cannot follow and the record can. Git's content addressing is the same idea for identity. Here is the joint where it breaks: git hashes content, and this system's addresses name three things content cannot express. A resolution, the grain of the pattern. A birth, the identity a being was given rather than the bytes it wears. And an act under a ground, a difference measured against a rebuilt null by a named recipe. Merkle hashing is kept as the holographic property; content is one argument of an address, never the whole of it.

[Koestler's holon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holon_(philosophy)), a whole to its parts and a part to its whole, is why the task layer is called `holon.js` and why the cube's grains nest.

On the language-model side the baseline is [retrieval-augmented generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.11401), and the cost side of the argument is the [lost-in-the-middle](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.03172) measurement that long prompts degrade a model's use of what is in them. [LLMLingua](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.05736) compresses tokens statistically where the holograph compresses by structure and stays exact. [MemGPT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.08560) pages memory in and out of a window under the model's control; here nothing is paged and nothing is under the model's control. [GraphRAG](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.16130) is the closest cousin, precomputed summaries over an entity graph. The differences are the ones the project has paid for: no model writes the summaries, they are templated from a checked ledger; identity is the index's rather than a string's; the cut is measured; and the addresses never reach the model.

That last list is where the claim lives. Every neighbour fails on one of those four. None of them is wrong about its own problem.

## 5. A holograph is only as true as its log

The warning in the repo is the one I trust most, because it came from the first build failing. A holograph is a projection, and a projection of the wrong reading is a compression of the wrong reading. No wall at the mouth's door can recover what the reader never heard.

The first holograph built its mention book from a presence index over capitalised runs, with no recurrence floor, rescanned at every turn. On Crime and Punishment, that index counts 333 "referents" over 4,570 sentences. The constitutional reader, the one the law says is the only writer of the log, establishes 113 beings and addresses 4,018 sentences. The 220 the presence index adds are the ones the reading law refuses: capitalised runs with no second occurrence, sentence openers, titles, "God Which." The fix was to project the address book from the reader's own log, in `reading-log.js`. The repo is candid that the page itself still ran the old presence index at the turn when it was written, so the page's holograph was, in its own phrase, the reading of the wrong reader. I could not check whether that has since closed.

There is a second class of failure that no re-expansion test catches. In one reading, a daughter and her father shared a final token and were folded into one referent with no witness required. Every address resolved, the bytes read back, the renders agreed. The receipts were valid and the oil was floating on seawater. A warehouse receipt system fails by issuing receipts for goods that were never in the warehouse, and drift detection catches an address whose bytes moved but has never been asked about an address whose reader was wrong. This is why the redealt-address control exists, and why its result matters more than any compression number: it asks whether the address does work or merely resolves.

## 6. The mechanical summary as the fold's heart

The repo's own warning about the pair is that a consumer who cannot re-expand has a summary, not a holograph, and the property lives in the pair. That sentence tells you what a mechanical summary is. It is the text half of the pair, the half a person or a mouth can read, computed from a record that holds the other half. Whether that half could be the heart of the fold depends on what the fold's heart is now, so start there.

**What the fold carries today.** `fold.js` states the claim it exists to make true: a conversation's context window does not grow with the conversation. Each turn is folded to what it contributed, and a running summary of roughly 200 characters (topic, flow, entities, context) is refreshed by one model call per turn. The file names that call as the one model call the fold spends. It calls this System 1, associative and lossy on purpose, and names its limit in its own comment: a paraphrase has no address, so "the report put the figure at 12%" and "the report put the figure at 21%" fold to the same line and nothing can tell them apart or get back to the source. System 2, the addressed record, exists because of that limit. An aperture gate skips the refresh on turns the engine's own continuation null says moved nothing, which is a way of rationing a call that probably should not be a call.

**What the proposal is.** Make the carried state a function of the record instead of a thing a model writes. The holograph document already says the Atmosphere block replaces the model-written summary at the answering turn. The proposal finishes that move for the carry itself. The record is the append-only log of every exchange with its referents resolved through the index, its cited addresses and its checked turns. The carried state is not stored. It is computed at a cursor, the way `foldAt` and the podcast builder's `renderEpisodeAt` already recompute a reading from the log's own entries sliced by sequence number, never cached forward from a later one.

The computed state has three parts at three grains, and each already exists as a function in `resolutions.js`. The Atmosphere reads the transcript as a stream of referent sets and cuts a new ground wherever a question names nothing the current ground held, and the cut is the REC. It says how long the conversation has stood on its current ground, where it turned, how many places it has cited, and whether the last exchange brought anything new. The Lens lists the ledger's notes about the active referents with their standing and disputes. The Paradigm lists the acts that recur between the same referents at the structural floor of two. Each is cut where widening stops changing the reach, with a declared ceiling named as a ceiling when no measurement fits. The text reaches the mouth with the addresses struck, and `cite.js` reattaches them afterwards.

**What that would change.** Four things follow, and I would trust them in this order. The carry costs zero model calls, which makes the aperture gate unnecessary, because the gate only existed to ration a call that no longer exists. The carry cannot drift. A model summary of a summary compounds its own errors, and the mechanical one is recomputed from the log every turn and never from itself. The carry becomes cursor-addressable, so the question what did the fold say at turn 12 has an answer by replay instead of by memory. And System 1 and System 2 stop being two stores. They become one object read at two grains, where the Atmosphere is the gist and the Lens lines are the part that can be reopened, and the difference `fold.js` draws between recalled and reopened becomes a difference in who holds the address. That last one is my synthesis, not something the repo says, and System 1's lossiness had a reason, since a gist is what a person retains. The Atmosphere is lossy too. The claim is that its loss is the right kind, exact and cut where nothing changes, rather than a paraphrase nobody can open.

**The skeleton-first turn.** The material side already has a worked example of the same idea. The generation pipeline builds a floor projection before any model touches the draft: the selected source sentences in outline order, composed with no model. The outline comes from `arrange.js`. The thesis is the general statement, no date and no figure, whose words recur across the most parts of the material. The body regroups statements by the beings they name, ordered by the dates they carry. A tension slot is filled only where the material itself marks a turn, and is a declared gap otherwise. A return slot has to come back to the thesis. Mechanical checks sit under all of it: each body group must bear on the thesis, consecutive groups are labelled succession, overlap or inversion, conflicting figures for the same relation are flagged and not merged, and circular chains are found. The pipeline's own comment states the consequence, that every model call after the floor can only improve on a product that is already true.

**What the pilot says.** The Sept 25 pilot is informal, two documents, not preregistered, and its own write-up says so. Fabrication came back clean on every arm, so fabrication did not discriminate anything. What discriminated was coverage, and it did not favour the pipeline. Asked to "summarize this document" with no stated length, the pipeline's selection dropped 14 of 19 outline slots on the Wikipedia article about the Great Pacific Garbage Patch, because an ask with no length reads as "write a short piece," and a bare 2B model with no scaffolding covered more in under half the time. On the narrative, O. Henry's "The Gift of the Magi," the arrangement grouped sections by the beings they were about and built them almost entirely from the opening scene, so the piece stops before Della sells her hair and never reaches the watch or the story's point.

The follow-up that matters most for this essay is the one that compared the floor with the full pipeline. On the article the floor was longer and more complete than the model's piece, 1,146 characters against 1,027 and nine sentences against six, and it kept the coordinates and the list of countries that the model's finishing pass compressed away in favour of editorializing the source did not contain. On the story the floor covered the same span as the model's piece without the one incoherent sentence the pass introduced. On this pilot, the free zero-model floor was never worse than the finished piece. The budgeted re-run says what the floor is not yet. With the length stated, selection kept 18 of 19 and 11 of 11 slots, and the outputs ran at 92 to 107 percent of the source length, which is a paraphrase and not a summary, at 3.3 to 4.7 times the model calls and 4.6 to 12 times the wall time. That run also exposed a quiet bug: the length parser read digits and the number words one through twelve, so "twenty" matched nothing and the pipeline fell back to its five-paragraph default without saying so, found only by reading the run logs line by line. And the scorer could not see two real defects in the model's budgeted pieces, a finding attributed to the wrong garbage patch and a dollar figure stated twice in a row. The floor is a safe lower bound. It is not yet a summary.

**Where it would fail.** I see three structural limits, and the first is checkable in the code. `mechanicalSummary` in `eval/eot-summary.mjs` takes the four referents with the highest degree in the material's notes and hands their Lens and Paradigm. That summarizes who is most connected, not what happened. There is no Atmosphere over the material in it. My notes from an earlier session record that the previous engine's fold returned cast lists instead of events on Kafka's Metamorphosis, so this is the same failure in a new engine, though I could not verify the earlier claim in this checkout. The repair is cheap in principle: the material has an atmosphere with re-zero points, the same segmentation the conversation gets, and a summary of a story is the sequence of its re-zeros. I did not check whether `exchangesOf` accepts passages instead of a transcript, so I do not know whether that is a call-site change or a new function.

The second limit is the one the mechanical route cannot cross. [Kintsch and van Dijk's macro-rules](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Kintsch) describe summarization as three operations: deletion, generalization and construction. The cut does deletion. The Paradigm does generalization, an act that recurs standing in for every occurrence. Construction is inferring a proposition no sentence states, and the point of a story is such a proposition. The Magi floor stops before the hair is sold, and the pilot's unscaffolded baseline named the whole arc and generic theme while dropping every figure. That is the two arms each missing one half. The repo's Generate cells are its thinnest, one of the 33 declared capacities runnable, and the hyperlexicon is the only worked example, grounded by a named giver. So the honest ceiling of a mechanical summary is deletion plus generalization. Anything that constructs has to enter as a proposal a gate can refuse, and the repo already carries a spec for exactly that, in which attention may propose and the record disposes. I have not checked whether it has been wired.

The third limit is silence. The Lens is only as full as the relation reader's recall, and that reader hears a fraction of what a passage states. A model's smoothing hides gaps. A mechanical summary with gaps looks authoritative, which is worse. The mechanism for this is already in the code, typed gaps rendered where a reading failed and declared voids with a scope, and a mechanical summary that does not carry its own "not heard" lines has made itself a more confident object than it has earned.

**Prior art, at the joints.** Extractive summarization from [Luhn in 1958](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Automatic_summarization) through [TextRank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TextRank) selects sentences by frequency and centrality, and fails by dangling anaphora and by having no notion of standing or of what the reader already holds. The floor shares the first failure, since source sentences lifted out of context can dangle, and the Lens is the answer to the second. [Rhetorical structure theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhetorical_structure_theory) is the family `arrange.js` belongs to, a schema for how parts of a text bear on one another, and the joint is that RST relations are annotated by people while the checks here are mechanical and mostly temporal. Hearst's [TextTiling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Text_segmentation) segments by shifts in lexical cohesion, and the Atmosphere segments by referent-set sharing and calls the cut a re-zero with a named act. And [recursive summarization for dialogue memory](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.15022) is the model-written System 1 almost exactly. Its joint is the one already named: a summary of a summary drifts, where a carry recomputed from the log cannot.

**What would show it.** I found no run in the checkout that carries a conversation with a purely mechanical summary against the model-refreshed one. The nearest is the aperture-gate eval, which compares a gated refresh with an ungated one and so measures how many model calls to spend on System 1, not whether System 1 should exist. The experiment is plain. Run one 25-turn transcript through two carriers, System 1 with the model refresh and the mechanical Atmosphere, Lens and Paradigm at each cursor, same mouth, and measure unsupported claims, re-asks, characters carried and calls per turn. The prediction I would register is that calls drop by exactly the refresh calls, that follow-ups naming no referent do at least as well because activation binds them to the last answer's, and that the mechanical carry does worse on turns that rest on the gist of what the person was trying to do, which referent sets do not hold. If that last prediction fails in the other direction, the carry has been understating itself.

## 7. Why it is omnimodal in EOT

The repo says "omnimodal by construction," and the sentence deserves a harder look than it gets, because most things called omnimodal are text systems with attachments.

Start with what the three properties actually require. Every one of them is a statement about addresses. A part points at the whole through an address; abstraction compresses by one address standing for many; the consumer is denied the address. Nothing in that is about words. What the properties need from a medium is only that its material can be addressed so the address reads back. The reading spec makes this the kernel's rule: an arrangement has ends, not parts of speech, and the kernel never speaks a medium's grammar. Subject and object, verbs, adjacency, those live in the text adapter, "medium-specific by construction." The kernel was measured going dark on anything a text adapter had not labelled, and the repair was to take participants by ordinal position and make role a caller-declared annotation the kernel never interprets. The notation that results, EOT, carries ends, labels and addresses, and that is the whole interface a medium owes it.

The adapters show what an address becomes when the medium changes. In MIDI the address is the event's ordinal and its tick, every note is declared by the file's own bytes, and a file whose chunks do not read back is refused with its reason rather than half parsed. For audio, the perceiver turns PCM into per-frame chroma, timbre and moment vectors and stops there; onsets, beats and segmentation are the engine's to find, not the perceiver's. For an image, a scanline order stands in for time, and the address of a visual claim is a normalized region, `<image>#x0,y0-x1,y1`, which the code refuses if it is degenerate or out of bounds, the same discipline P5.2 holds for byte ranges. And the podcast builder shows the holograph working as a property of the ledger rather than of text: the whole reading is recomputed from the log at any cursor, never cached forward from a later sequence number.

Two smaller details are the strongest evidence that the claim is a design and not a slogan. The return-curve measurement knows only events, positions and discovered form labels, so a leitmotif returning and a pronoun returning are the same curve to it, pinned by a music case in its tests with no kernel change. And the text face declares its script per sentence in the EOT reading, so a document that mixes English and Mandarin says which sentences the capitalisation mechanism can and cannot see, instead of averaging into one number. A system that is omnilingual only by accident would never need that field. The `[A-Z]` scan the first holograph used would have handed a Russian reader an empty Atmosphere with no refusal on the record. Medium blindness is a property the kernel has to earn against exactly that kind of silent English default.

Now the limits, because the strongest form of the claim is not yet supported. What is omnimodal is the log and the address, not yet the Lens. The Lens, Paradigm and Atmosphere blocks are computed from the relation reader's claims, and the only relation reader built is the text one. The repo's own sentence, that a Lens over a score or a film shot renders the same way, is a nomination, and the document says nominations lose disagreements with the code. I looked for a run of the compression ladder over non-text material and found none. I did find the image-concepts organ, which lands visual facts on the same ledger as everything else, but its own header says the region addresses were verified by direct visual inspection before landing, with the method disclosed on every note, because no automated re-slice check exists for a screenshot region. That is an honest raster analogue of an address that reads back, and it is not yet the mechanical one. A holograph whose addresses are checked by a person is closer to a signed receipt than to a plate.

So the precise claim is this. The holograph is omnimodal at the level where the kernel lives: ends, labels, addresses, a grain, a birth. It is medium-blind there by a rule that was tested against a music case and a mixed-script case. It is not yet demonstrated at the level where the mouth lives, where a claim has to be read out of the medium before it can be handed down. The honest unit of omnimodality is one adapter that can say, in the medium's own terms, what a recurring act between two referents is.

## 8. What would refute it

Four conditions, in order of how cheaply they could be run.

If the redealt-address control fails, that is, if addresses assigned at random reach the same reading quality as the real ones, the holograph is a compression discipline with decorative provenance, and the pair of the address and the reading is not doing the work I have claimed. The doc lists this run as pending, so it is the first thing to look at.

If the compression ladder is not monotone, if a higher rung needs more than the rung below to settle the same question, then abstraction has failed, which the doc itself names as the abstraction's fault rather than the consumer's.

If the mechanical summary cannot reach the second half of a story, the claim that it could be the fold's heart fails for narrative. The Magi test is the instrument for it: give the summary an Atmosphere over the material, run it on the story again, and check whether it reaches the sale of the hair and the exchange of gifts. If it still stops in the opening scene, then the mechanical summary is a document instrument, good for material whose parts bear on a thesis, and the fold's carry for conversation stands on weaker evidence than section 6 suggests. A related failure would be the carry losing to System 1 on follow-ups that rest on gist. If it only ties, the gain is the removed model call and the removed drift, which is still a reason to make it the heart, but then the argument is operational and not epistemic, and I would say so.

And if no non-text Lens can be built without borrowing the text relation reader, then the omnimodality in the name belongs to the ledger and not to the reading, and "omnimodal by construction" should be struck back to "omnimodal in the log." The cheapest test is the one the MIDI adapter was built to host, a short corpus where every event has an address that reads back and nothing has to be pitch tracked: read it, project a Paradigm line for a recurring act, hand it to a mouth with the addresses struck, and check that the record can reopen it to ticks. If that works once, the claim moves from a nomination to a result. If it needs a human in the loop to say what the act was, the holograph is still a good idea about addresses and not yet an idea about reading.
